name: Midsummer Night Music Festival Finale
blurb: Closing night of St. Armands Key Lutheran Church's summer concert series: soprano Michelle Giglio sings arias, art songs and Great American Songbook standards a block off the Circle. Tickets $20-$30 at the door, or stream it online for $10.

name: As You Like It (The Sarasota Players, 97th Season Opener)
venue: The Sarasota Players at The Crossings at Siesta Key
address: 3501 S Tamiami Trail, Suite 1130, Sarasota, FL 34239
dates_label: Opens Thu, Sep 17 · runs through Sep 27
hours_label: Evenings 7:30 PM, matinees 2 PM · Tickets via box office
blurb: The Sarasota Players, the area's oldest theatre company, opens its 97th season with Shakespeare's pastoral comedy of disguise and romance in the Forest of Arden. Performances at the company's home in The Crossings at Siesta Key; park and enter by Connors Steak & Seafood. Tickets through the box office (941-365-2494).

name: Echoes of Sarasota: Opening Reception
blurb: Free opening reception for the city's new cultural heritage exhibit: 19 mural-scale paintings by Regan Dunnick, Frank Hopper and others tracing more than 1,000 years of regional history, 16 of them hanging at City Hall. Light refreshments, with welcoming remarks at 4:30 PM on Constitution Day. The exhibit stays on view during regular City Hall hours afterward.
photo_credit: Photo: Your Observer / City of Sarasota

name: Sarasota Farmers Market
address: Lemon Ave & Main St, Sarasota, FL 34236
blurb: Sarasota's signature Saturday ritual since 1979: 70-plus vendors along Lemon Avenue and Main Street with local produce, fresh seafood, baked goods, plants and live music. Free to browse; bring a tote and arrive early before the heat. Dog friendly.

name: St. Armands Circle Art Festival with Craft Marketplace
hours_label: 10 AM - 5 PM both days · Free admission
blurb: Howard Alan Events' 4th annual juried festival fills the Circle with fine art in the park and a craft marketplace along the street: paintings, glass, jewelry, photography and more from local and national artists. Free to browse, about 22,000 visitors expected; pair it with brunch on the Circle and a Lido Beach afternoon.
photo_credit: Photo: Howard Alan Events / Your Observer
